title: NEWS2, escalation and Martha's Rule
blurb: Score NEWS2 accurately, match the score to the right response and monitoring frequency, escalate with SBAR, and know how Martha's Rule works.
question: Mrs Agyeman, 66, has pneumonia and is on 2 L/min oxygen. Her observations: RR 23, SpO2 94%, BP 104/70, pulse 102, alert, temperature 38.4 °C. What is her NEWS2 and what response does it require?

teach.body: The National Early Warning Score 2 (RCP 2017) is a track-and-trigger tool: six physiological parameters are each scored 0–3, oxygen adds 2, and the total guides how urgently and by whom the person is reviewed and how often they are observed. It is for adults aged 16 or over and is not used in pregnancy. It supports, and never replaces, clinical judgement: any concern should prompt review, and the trend matters as much as the total.

head: Parameter
teach.caption: Low values on the left, high on the right. New confusion (C) scores 3, the same as V, P or U.

bands.label: Medium: key threshold for urgent response

head: NEWS2
Minimum observations
Response
rows: Registered nurse decides on frequency or escalation
RN informs medical team at once; urgent review; monitored setting
RN informs team at once (at least registrar); critical care team assessment
teach.caption: At 7 or more, consider transfer to level 2 or 3 care. Any concern about a person overrides the score.

teach.h: SpO2 Scale 2 is prescribed, not chosen
teach.body: Scale 2 is for people with hypercapnic respiratory failure who have a prescribed target of 88–92%, usually some people with COPD. The decision to use it is made by a competent clinical decision maker and recorded in the notes. On Scale 2, 88–92% (or 93% or more on air) scores 0, but 93–94% on oxygen scores 1, 95–96% on oxygen 2 and 97% or more on oxygen 3, because too much oxygen is harmful. Everyone else uses Scale 1.

teach.h: Worked example: Mrs Agyeman on a respiratory ward
items: RR 23 scores 2. SpO2 94% on Scale 1 scores 1. Oxygen at 2 L/min scores 2.
BP 104/70 scores 1. Pulse 102 scores 1. Alert scores 0. Temperature 38.4 °C scores 1.
Response: continuous monitoring; the registered nurse informs the medical team immediately (at least specialist registrar) and requests emergency assessment by a team with critical care skills.
She calls using SBAR and, because infection is suspected, flags sepsis: NICE NG253 treats a NEWS2 of 7 or more as high risk.

letters.word: Situation: who you are, who the patient is, the concern
Recommendation: what you need and by when

teach.h: Martha's Rule: the three core components
head: Component
What it means
rows: Patients are asked at least daily how they feel and whether they are getting better or worse; this is acted on
Any staff member can, at any time, ask for a review from a different team if concerned and not responded to
Patients, families and carers can call for a rapid review by a different team, advertised across the hospital
teach.caption: NHS England. It is not a second opinion. The NHS Standard Contract 2026/27 requires the three components in adult and paediatric inpatient settings by 31 March 2027.

teach.text: Three classic slips: a single parameter scoring 3 triggers an urgent ward-based response even if the total is low; Scale 2 is used only once prescribed by a competent decision maker; and Martha's Rule is a rapid review for deterioration, not a second opinion on a diagnosis.

items: Six parameters plus 2 for oxygen; adults 16+, not pregnancy; supports judgement.
0: 12-hourly. 1–4: 4–6-hourly, RN decides. Single 3: hourly, inform medical team.
5–6: hourly, inform at once, urgent review. 7+: continuous, emergency critical care assessment.
Scale 2 only when a 88–92% target is prescribed and recorded.
SBAR for escalation; Martha's Rule lets staff, patients and families call a rapid review by a different team.

summary: You can now score NEWS2 on Scale 1 and Scale 2, match each threshold to the right observation frequency and response, and escalate clearly with SBAR. You understand Martha's Rule and how patients, families and staff can call for a rapid review.

A.q: Mr Ellis, 58, is on air. RR 19, SpO2 95%, BP 108/72, pulse 88, alert, temperature 37.2 °C. What is his NEWS2?
A.why: SpO2 95% scores 1 and systolic BP 108 scores 1; all other parameters score 0, so the total is 2.

whyNot.0: This misses one of the two scoring parameters: SpO2 94–95% and systolic 101–110 each score 1.
whyNot.2: No parameter scores 2 or more; the total is 2, not 3.
whyNot.3: SpO2 95% and BP 108 both score 1, so the total cannot be 0.

A.q: A patient's NEWS2 is 3, made up of three parameters each scoring 1. What is the minimum frequency of observations?
A.why: NEWS2 Chart 4: a total of 1–4 (without a single parameter scoring 3) needs a minimum of 4–6-hourly observations, with the registered nurse deciding on frequency or escalation.

whyNot.1: Hourly is for a single parameter scoring 3 or a total of 5 or more.
whyNot.2: 12-hourly is the minimum for a score of 0.
whyNot.3: Continuous monitoring is for a total of 7 or more.

A.q: For which of these people should NEWS2 not be used?
options: A woman who is 30 weeks pregnant
A.why: The RCP says NEWS should not be used in children under 16 or in women who are pregnant, because their physiological response to illness is modified.

whyNot.0: NEWS2 applies to adults of any age; new confusion is scored, though dementia needs careful interpretation.
whyNot.2: People aged 16 or over are within NEWS2's scope.
whyNot.3: NEWS2 applies; Scale 2 may be used if a target of 88–92% is prescribed.

B.q: Ms Novak, 49, on air, has a pulse of 132. Every other parameter scores 0. What response does NEWS2 require?
options: Emergency critical care team review now
12-hourly observations, as the total is low
B.why: A pulse of 131 or more scores 3. A single parameter scoring 3 is low-medium risk: an urgent ward-based response, minimum hourly observations, and the RN informs the medical team.

whyNot.0: A single red score of 3 overrides the routine 1–4 frequency.
whyNot.2: Emergency critical care assessment is the response to a total of 7 or more.
whyNot.3: 12-hourly is for a total of 0; a single 3 needs hourly observations.

B.q: Who should decide that a patient's oxygen saturation is to be scored on SpO2 Scale 2?
options: The patient, based on their home oxygen
Any nurse who knows the patient has COPD
The healthcare assistant doing the observations
B.why: RCP NEWS2 rec 26: the decision to use Scale 2 should be made by a competent clinical decision maker and recorded in the notes, with a prescribed 88–92% target.

whyNot.1: The patient's history informs the decision, but a clinician makes and records it.
whyNot.2: Not everyone with COPD is at risk of hypercapnic failure; a diagnosis by itself does not justify Scale 2.
whyNot.3: Recording observations does not include deciding which scale to use.

B.q: A staff nurse is worried that Mr Ahmed is deteriorating. She has raised it twice with his team and feels she is not being responded to. Under Martha's Rule, what can she do?
options: Wait for the consultant's ward round tomorrow
Ask his family to make a formal complaint
Request a rapid review from a different team
Arrange a second opinion on his diagnosis
B.why: Martha's Rule: all staff can, at any time, ask for a review from a different team if concerned that a patient is deteriorating and they are not being responded to.

whyNot.0: Waiting delays the review Martha's Rule is designed to provide now.
whyNot.1: A complaint is not an escalation route for acute deterioration.
whyNot.3: NHS England is clear that Martha's Rule is not a second opinion.

C.q: Mrs Agyeman, 66, has pneumonia and is on 2 L/min oxygen. RR 23, SpO2 94%, BP 104/70, pulse 102, alert, temperature 38.4 °C. What response does her NEWS2 require?
options: Half-hourly observations; review on ward round
C.why: Her NEWS2 is 8 (RR 2, SpO2 1, oxygen 2, BP 1, pulse 1, temperature 1). 7 or more requires continuous monitoring, immediate escalation to at least registrar level and emergency assessment by a team with critical care competencies.

whyNot.0: Hourly observations and urgent review fit a total of 5–6; hers is 8.
whyNot.3: No NEWS2 band waits for a ward round; 7 or more is an emergency response.

C.q: A nurse calls the doctor: 'This is Sam on Ward 7 about Mrs Lowe; I'm worried she is deteriorating. She came in 3 days ago with cellulitis. Her NEWS2 is 7, RR 26, BP 96/60, and I think she may have sepsis.' What should she say next to complete SBAR?
options: She has type 2 diabetes and takes metformin
Her temperature is 38.6 °C and pulse is 118
Please come and review her within 15 minutes
I'm calling from Ward 7 about Mrs Lowe
C.why: Situation, background and assessment have been given; the Recommendation states clearly what she needs and by when.

whyNot.0: This adds background, which has already been covered; it does not complete SBAR.
whyNot.1: More observations belong in the assessment, which she has given.
whyNot.3: This repeats the situation she opened with.

C.q: Which of these is one of the three core components of Martha's Rule?
options: Families may request a second opinion on a diagnosis
Patients score their own NEWS2 at least daily
Staff escalate to the same team three times first
Patients are asked daily if they feel better or worse
C.why: NHS England: patients will be asked at least daily how they are feeling and whether they are getting better or worse, and this is acted on in a structured way.

whyNot.0: Martha's Rule is explicitly not a second opinion process.
whyNot.1: Patients are asked how they feel; they do not calculate NEWS2.
whyNot.2: Staff may ask a different team at any time when concerned and not responded to; there is no set number of attempts.

reteach.title: Score, match, act
reteach.question: NEWS2 is three moves: what is the score, which band is it in, and what must happen now?

blocks.body: Score each parameter and add 2 for oxygen. Look for any single 3. Then match: 0 is 12-hourly; 1–4 is 4–6-hourly with the RN deciding; a single 3 or 5–6 means hourly and telling the medical team; 7 or more means continuous monitoring and an emergency response. Whatever the number, if you are worried, escalate.

blocks.h: As the score rises, the response tightens

blocks.text: Oxygen itself scores 2. A person whose saturation is 'fine' on 4 L/min has already used up two points.

explain.body: Respiration rate, SpO2, systolic BP, pulse, consciousness (ACVPU, including new confusion) and temperature; supplemental oxygen adds 2.

test.q: How many points does supplemental oxygen add to the NEWS2 total?
test.why: Receiving supplemental oxygen scores 2 on NEWS2.

whyNot.1: Oxygen scores 2; 3 is the maximum for a single physiological parameter.
whyNot.2: Oxygen always adds points; only breathing air scores 0.

explain.body: 0–4 low; a single 3 low-medium; 5–6 medium, the key threshold for urgent response; 7 or more high, needing an emergency response.

test.q: Which NEWS2 total is described as the key threshold for an urgent response?
test.why: NEWS2 Chart 2: an aggregate of 5–6 is medium risk and the key threshold for urgent response.

whyNot.1: 1–4 is low risk with a ward-based response.
whyNot.2: A total of 3 from several parameters is low risk; it is a single parameter of 3 that raises the response.
whyNot.3: 9 or more is within the high band that starts at 7.

explain.body: For prescribed 88–92% targets only. 88–92% scores 0; on oxygen, 93–94% scores 1, 95–96% scores 2 and 97% or more scores 3.

test.q: Mr Price is correctly on SpO2 Scale 2 and receiving oxygen. His saturation is 97%. What does it score?
test.why: On Scale 2, 97% or more on oxygen scores 3, signalling over-oxygenation risk in hypercapnic failure.

whyNot.0: 0 is for 88–92%, or 93% or more on air.

explain.body: Use SBAR: situation, background, assessment, recommendation. If concerns are not responded to, Martha's Rule lets staff, patients and families call a rapid review by a different team.

test.q: In SBAR, what does the 'A' stand for?
test.why: SBAR is Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation.

whyNot.0: What you want done is the Recommendation, not 'Action'.
whyNot.1: Allergies may be part of Background, but 'A' is Assessment.
whyNot.3: The admission reason belongs in Background.
